t: A Hellenistic kingdom on the southern Black Sea, ruled by a dynasty of Persian origin from Amaseia and later Sinope.
Rich in metals, timber and Greek ports, it built a Black Sea empire under Mithridates VI Eupator.
Mithridates VI fought Rome in three wars from 89 to 63 BCE before Pompey destroyed the kingdom.
dyk: The geographer Strabo was born at Amaseia, the first Pontic capital, around 64 BCE, into a family that had served the kings of Pontus.
ev: Mithridates I Ktistes takes the title of king
Pharnaces I captures Sinope and makes it his capital
Diophantus brings Chersonesus and the Bosporan Kingdom under Pontic rule
Mithridates VI overruns Roman Asia and orders the massacre of Romans and Italians
Peace of Dardanus ends the First Mithridatic War
Lucullus defeats Mithridates at Cabira and occupies Pontus
Pompey routs Mithridates on the Lycus river
Mithridates VI dies at Panticapaeum; Pompey divides Pontus

f.successor: Roman Republic (province of Bithynia et Pontus); Polemonid Pontus
